label: DrayTek VigorSwitch VSP2100-K 8-port PoE+ gigabit switch
description: DrayTek VigorSwitch VSP2100-K - passively cooled 1U managed Layer 2+ switch with 8x 10/100/1000BASE-T PoE+ ports (802.3at, 30 W per port, 140 W aggregate budget), 2x 1000BASE-X SFP uplinks and an RJ45 console port. 802.1Q VLANs with voice and surveillance profiles, 802.1x/TACACS+ authentication, ACLs, ONVIF camera management, cloud managed via VigorACS or standalone.
notes: The port census is quoted ('8 RJ-45 Ethernet Ports - 10/100/1000Mbps', '2 SFP Ports - 1000Mbps', 'Console Port (RJ-45 physical, RS-232 electrical)'), and so is the power story: **PoE+ on all 8 ports, 140 W budget**, with 164.3 W maximum input consumption - so the budget is real and not the PSU rating, which is the distinction that matters on this part. **One contradiction recorded rather than resolved:** the product is sold as VSP2100-K, the specification heading on the same page says 'VSP2121-K', and the body text repeatedly calls it 'VigorSwitch P2100' and quotes P2100 and G2100 figures side by side. The 8-port PoE chassis (P2100) numbers are the ones used here, because they are the ones attached to the PoE budget; the model string kept is the one the page sells and the request names. Layer 2+ with VLAN routing and static routes justifies `l3-forward`; the console port is declared as console, not as Ethernet.
